mainTopic: Which blemishes permit slaughtering a בכור, which defects do not, and whether an אנדרוגינוס counts as blemished
overview: This amud moves through several short units about blemishes on a בכור. A ברייתא first explains which leg joint the previous משנה meant for a calf's tail. A new משנה then says that all the listed blemishes allow a בכור to be slaughtered and פסולי המוקדשין to be redeemed. The גמרא explains that this repeated line is a סתם משנה that confirms the הלכה follows even single Sages' opinions. A further משנה lists problems that do not permit slaughter anywhere: temporary blemishes, old, sick, or foul-smelling animals, and animals tied to a sin known only through one witness or the owner. The גמרא resolves the conflict over גרב and חזזית by splitting them into curable and incurable kinds, ending with three kinds of גרב. It then finds Torah sources for disqualifying old, sick, foul-smelling, and sin-related animals, and shows why each exclusion is needed. Finally it asks why an אנדרוגינוס is not considered blemished by its female organ. אביי and רבא each prove that a crack in flesh is not a מום, and the גמרא explains how the dissenting תנא disagrees with both.

steps.title: Which joint the calf's tail must reach
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא clarifies that the joint mentioned in the משנה is the upper joint, not the lower one. It adds that this joint is easy to see on a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the joint meant is the upper joint, not the lower joint. The matching bone on a camel can be clearly seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to define a word from the previous משנה. That משנה discussed a calf whose tail does not reach the joint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה said a calf's tail should reach the joint, but a leg has more than one joint. The ברייתא says the upper joint is meant. Since that joint is hard to see on a calf, it points to a camel, where the matching joint stands out clearly.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught: the upper joint
phrases.notes: This refers to the joint from the previous משנה about a calf's tail.

phrases.english: and not the lower joint,
and the matching joint on a camel is easy to see.
phrases.notes: On a calf this joint is hidden, so the camel is used as a reference point.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: קֶפֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹן וְלֹא קֶפֶץ הַתַּחְתּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defines a term from the previous משנה, which is not part of this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The joint in the calf's-tail blemish is the upper joint. On a camel, this joint is easy to see.

steps.title: All these blemishes allow slaughter and redemption
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that every blemish listed so far allows a בכור to be slaughtered outside the מקדש. It also allows פסולי המוקדשין to be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of these blemishes, one may slaughter the firstborn animal, and disqualified sacrificial animals may be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: A short new משנה gives one summary rule that covers all the blemishes listed in the earlier משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור cannot be offered, so it may be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש. An animal that was set aside as a קרבן and then became blemished may be exchanged for money, which is called פדיון. The משנה says each listed blemish counts for both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes that disqualify an animal from being a קרבן
A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth
Sacrificial animals that became disqualified, for example by a blemish
They are redeemed, meaning their holiness is moved onto money

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Because of these blemishes
phrases.notes: This means all the blemishes listed in the earlier משניות.

phrases.english: one may slaughter the firstborn,
and disqualified sacrificial animals may be redeemed because of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens a new משנה after the ברייתא's definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed blemishes allow a בכור to be slaughtered and פסולי המוקדשין to be redeemed.

steps.title: Why repeat what the chapter already said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the opening of the פרק already said a בכור may be slaughtered because of these blemishes. So why say it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this again? The first clause already taught: because of these blemishes one may slaughter the firstborn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating itself. The beginning of the פרק already said the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the משנה does not waste words. The words about the בכור match the opening line of the פרק exactly. So this repetition seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this again?
The first clause, here the opening of the פרק

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need this again?
He already taught it in the first clause:
phrases.notes: This refers to the opening line of the פרק.

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר!
phrases.english: Because of these blemishes one may slaughter the firstborn!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the משנה in step 2 for repeating itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first half of the משנה, about slaughtering a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening of the פרק already says the exact same thing, so the repetition seems pointless.

steps.title: The new point is redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the second half is the real new point: פסולי המוקדשין may be redeemed because of these blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter clause was needed: disqualified sacrificial animals may be redeemed because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the משנה. It says the משנה only repeated the בכור line in order to add the new law about redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening of the פרק spoke only about a בכור. Redemption of פסולי המוקדשין was not mentioned there. So the second half seems to add something new.

phrases.english: The latter clause was needed:
disqualified sacrificial animals may be redeemed because of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the focus to a different clause that carries the new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה just repeats the opening of the פרק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The new point is the redemption of פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: Redemption is obvious too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. If a blemish is serious enough to allow slaughtering a holy בכור, it surely allows redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious: if we may slaughter because of it, do we need to be told that we may redeem?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. It says redemption follows automatically from slaughter, so it also does not need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a בכור and eating it outside the מקדש is a bigger step than redeeming a disqualified animal. If the blemish allows the bigger step, it obviously allows the smaller one. So the second half adds nothing new, and the original question comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it needed to say? (meaning: of course not)

phrases.english: This too is obvious:
if we may slaughter because of it,
do we need to be told that we may redeem?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. Of course redemption is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4, that the redemption clause is the new point
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a blemish allows slaughtering a בכור, it obviously allows redemption, so the clause is still unnecessary.
steps.confusionAlert: Grammatically this is a question, but in function it is a challenge. It knocks down step 4 and brings back the original question from step 3, which step 6 then answers.

steps.title: An anonymous ruling to confirm the minority opinions
steps.stepSummary: The real reason for the line: earlier משניות included blemishes taught by single Sages, which might seem not to be the הלכה. So the משנה states one anonymous ruling that covers all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the earlier משנה taught that אילא added three blemishes and the Sages said they had not heard of them. It then went on to teach opinions of individual Sages. So the משנה states one anonymous ruling covering all of them: because of these blemishes one may slaughter the firstborn, and disqualified sacrificial animals may be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The line is not new information. It is a stamp that confirms the הלכה follows all the blemishes listed, including the disputed ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אילא added three blemishes and the Sages said 'we did not hear of these.' After that, the משנה cited single opinions such as רבי חנניה בן גמליאל and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. Rulings from one person usually do not become הלכה, so by repeating the rule as a סתם משנה, the משנה shows that the הלכה follows them.

keyTerms.meaning: We did not hear (of this from our teachers)
A single Sage's opinion, a minority view
States it anonymously, without naming who said it

steps.whatToRemember: The summary line in the משנה looks repetitive, but its job is to make the rule a סתם משנה. This tells us the הלכה follows every blemish listed, even those first taught by a single Sage or doubted by the Sages.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle for ruling on משנה: an anonymous ruling (סתם משנה) can turn an individual's opinion into accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: Rather, since it taught
'he added three,'
phrases.notes: This refers to אילא, who added three blemishes in an earlier משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: and they said to him: we did not hear of these,
and it went on to teach individual opinions,
phrases.notes: These include רבי חנניה בן גמליאל and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

phrases.english: so it states the rule anonymously about all of them:

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
phrases.english: because of these blemishes one may slaughter the firstborn
and disqualified sacrificial animals may be redeemed because of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives a new answer to the question in step 3, after step 5 rejected the first answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the repetition by its purpose: confirming the הלכה through an anonymous ruling, not adding new content
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The single-Sage blemishes, and the ones the Sages doubted, might not be the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The anonymous summary confirms that the הלכה follows all of the listed blemishes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The repeated line exists to state the rule as a סתם משנה covering every listed blemish, which confirms the minority opinions as הלכה.

steps.title: Blemishes that do not allow slaughtering a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists blemishes and conditions that do not permit slaughtering a בכור, neither in the מקדש nor outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the blemishes for which we do not slaughter a בכור, neither in the מקדש nor in the rest of the country: pale spots on the eye; tears that are not constant; inner gums that were damaged but not uprooted; an animal with גרב, with warts, or with חזזית; an old, sick, or foul-smelling animal; an animal used for a sin; or one that killed a person, when this is known only from one witness or from the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous משנה listed real blemishes. Now a new משנה lists the opposite: weak, temporary, or unproven problems that do NOT allow a בכור to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These problems are either temporary (they may heal) or are not bodily blemishes at all (old, sick, smelly). Many of them still keep the animal off the מזבח, so it cannot be offered in the מקדש, yet none is a מום that permits slaughter outside. In the last two cases, one witness or the owner is enough to disqualify the animal from the מזבח, but not enough to have it put to death.

keyTerms.meaning: A pale or white spot on the eye
A type of boil or skin eruption
Another type of skin boil or rash
Based on only a single witness

steps.confusionAlert: "Not in the מקדש and not in the country" does NOT mean the animal is fine. Most of these animals may not be offered on the מזבח (see steps 17 and 21 for the sources). Yet their problem is not a מום that permits slaughtering a בכור outside, so the בכור is stuck both ways.

phrases.english: MISHNA
And these are the ones for which one does not slaughter
neither in the Temple nor in the country:
pale spots, and tears that are not constant,
and inner gums that were damaged
but not ones that were uprooted,
and one with garav boils, and one with warts,
and one with chazazit boils,
an old one, a sick one, a foul-smelling one,
and one with which a sin was committed,
and one that killed a person

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבְּעָלִים.
phrases.english: based on one witness or based on the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן, לֹא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ וְלֹא בַּמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It contrasts with the earlier list of real blemishes that do allow slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Temporary, non-bodily, or unproven defects do not allow a בכור to be slaughtered anywhere.

steps.title: The dispute about a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: A טומטום or אנדרוגינוס is not slaughtered anywhere. רבי שמעון says it is the greatest blemish. חכמים say it is not a בכור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס is not slaughtered, neither in the מקדש nor in the country. רבי שמעון says: There is no blemish greater than this. חכמים say: It is not a בכור at all. Rather, it may be shorn and used for work.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a special case: an animal whose gender is hidden or doubled. It records a מחלוקת about its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening ruling treats this animal as one that cannot be slaughtered as a blemished בכור. רבי שמעון disagrees: it is a בכור, and its odd body is a major blemish, so it may be slaughtered. חכמים go the other way: a בכור must be clearly male, so this animal has no holiness and is like ordinary חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose sexual organs are hidden
An animal with both male and female organs
May be shorn and used for work (signs of ordinary חולין status)

phrases.english: And a tumtum and a hermaphrodite,
neither in the Temple nor in the country.
Rabbi Shimon says:
You have no blemish greater than this,
and the Rabbis say: It is not a firstborn,
rather it is shorn and worked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, לֹא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ וְלֹא בַּמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a disputed special case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first ruling: not slaughtered anywhere. רבי שמעון: it is a great blemish and may be slaughtered. חכמים: it has no בכור holiness at all.

steps.title: The Torah lists גרב and ילפת as blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say גרב and חזזית are not blemishes when the Torah lists גרב and ילפת as blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is גרב not a blemish? But the Torah writes "גרב"! And is חזזית not a blemish? But the Torah writes "ילפת"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from a פסוק (ויקרא כב:כב) that lists גרב and ילפת among the blemishes that disqualify an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גרב question is direct: the same word appears in the Torah's list. The חזזית question rests on the claim that ילפת means חזזית. The next step brings the source for that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
A skin disease listed among blemishes in the Torah

phrases.english: GEMARA
And is garav not a blemish?
But isn't "garav" written in the Torah!
And is chazazit not a blemish?
But isn't "yalefet" written in the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה's inclusion of גרב and חזזית in the list of non-blemishes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that גרב and חזזית do not allow slaughtering a בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah explicitly names גרב and ילפת (חזזית) as blemishes. A משנה cannot call a Torah-listed blemish a non-blemish.

steps.title: Proof that ילפת is the Egyptian חזזית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא identifies גרב as חרס and ילפת as חזזית המצרית. ריש לקיש explains that ילפת clings until death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: "גרב" is חרס (hard boils). "ילפת" is the Egyptian חזזית. And ריש לקיש said: Why is it called ילפת? Because it keeps clinging until the day of death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its challenge. It shows that the Torah's ילפת really is a kind of חזזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source supports the question, but it also hides the answer. The ברייתא says the Torah means the Egyptian kind of חזזית specifically. ריש לקיש adds that this kind never heals, which is why it counts as a permanent blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: The Egyptian chazazit (the boils of the plague in Egypt)

steps.whyThisMatters: The word "Egyptian" and the idea of "until death" (it cannot heal) set up the coming answer. A permanent problem is a real blemish. A temporary one is not.

phrases.english: And it is taught: "Garav" is the cheres (hard boils),
"Yalefet" is the Egyptian chazazit,
and Reish Lakish said:
Why is it called "yalefet"?
Because it keeps clinging until the day of death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source showing that ילפת equals חזזית, which strengthens the קשיא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the Torah's ילפת is a form of חזזית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (ילפת = חזזית המצרית) and ריש לקיש (it clings until death).

steps.title: Egyptian חזזית versus ordinary חזזית
steps.stepSummary: The חזזית contradiction is easy to solve. The Torah means the Egyptian kind, and the משנה means the ordinary kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, חזזית against חזזית is no difficulty: here the Torah speaks of Egyptian חזזית, and there the משנה speaks of ordinary חזזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers half of the challenge. It solves the חזזית contradiction using the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's ילפת is the incurable Egyptian חזזית, so it is a real blemish. The משנה is talking about ordinary חזזית, which can heal, so it is not a full blemish. Both sources are correct, each about a different kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is fine (sets up the part that is still hard)

phrases.english: Granted, chazazit against chazazit is not difficult:
here it is the Egyptian chazazit,
there it is an ordinary chazazit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 10 to resolve the חזזית half of the קשיא in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (Egyptian vs. ordinary חזזית)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah and the משנה seemed to argue about the same חזזית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah means the incurable Egyptian kind, and the משנה means the ordinary, curable kind.

steps.title: The גרב contradiction remains
steps.stepSummary: The גרב contradiction still stands, because the ברייתא gave no special kind of גרב to split.
steps.simpleTranslation: But גרב against גרב is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the גרב half of the question has not been answered yet. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חזזית, the ברייתא gave us two kinds (Egyptian and ordinary). For גרב, the Torah and the משנה use the exact same word, and no such split has been offered. So the contradiction still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the part that is still a problem)

phrases.english: But garav against garav is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא… אלא pattern: חזזית is solved, but גרב is still a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that גרב is not a blemish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah uses the very same word, גרב, as a blemish, and there is no known split between two kinds of גרב.

steps.title: Moist גרב heals, dry גרב does not
steps.stepSummary: The גרב contradiction is solved too. The משנה means moist גרב, which heals. The Torah means dry גרב, which does not heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: גרב against גרב is also no difficulty: this one is moist, and that one is dry. Moist גרב heals. Dry גרב does not heal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the remaining contradiction by splitting גרב into two kinds, just as it did with חזזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moist גרב can be cured, so it is only a temporary problem and does not allow slaughtering a בכור. That is the משנה's case. Dry גרב is permanent, so it is a real blemish. That is the Torah's case.
steps.whatToRemember: The key test for a blemish is permanence. Only a blemish that will not heal (Egyptian חזזית, dry גרב) allows a בכור to be slaughtered. A curable version (ordinary חזזית, moist גרב) does not.

phrases.english: Garav against garav is also not difficult:
this is moist, that is dry.
Moist heals,
dry does not heal.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּרָב אַגָּרָב נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּלַח, הָא בְּיָבֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the remaining גרב contradiction from step 12 using the same split method as step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (moist vs. dry גרב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah and the משנה seemed to disagree about the same גרב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means moist, curable גרב (a temporary problem). The Torah means dry, incurable גרב (a permanent blemish).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both skin conditions are real blemishes only in their incurable forms. Their curable forms are the ones the משנה lists as non-blemishes.

steps.title: Does moist skin disease really heal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the last answer. A פסוק in דברים says moist גרב cannot be healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does moist גרב really heal? But the פסוק says: 'God will strike you with the boil of Egypt, and with גרב, and with חרס, which you cannot be healed from.' Since the פסוק lists חרס separately, the גרב in that פסוק must be the moist kind. Yet the פסוק says it cannot be healed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 13, which said moist גרב heals. It brings a פסוק showing that moist גרב does not heal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already taught that the Torah's גרב for blemishes is חרס, the dry kind. The פסוק in דברים lists גרב and חרס side by side, so its גרב must be a different kind, the moist one. That פסוק says 'you cannot be healed,' so the claim that moist גרב heals seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof works only because חרס appears in the same פסוק. חרס is the dry kind, so the גרב listed next to it must be the moist kind.

phrases.english: And does a moist one heal?
But isn't it written: 'God will strike you with the boil of Egypt, etc.'
And since it is written 'and with חרס'
the גרב in that verse must mean moist גרב
phrases.notes: חרס is dry, so the separate גרב must be the moist kind.

phrases.english: and it says: 'which you cannot be healed from'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that moist גרב heals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק lists moist גרב, as distinct from חרס, among diseases that cannot be healed.

steps.title: There are three kinds of גרב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are three kinds of גרב. Each one is either dry or moist, on the inside and on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there are three kinds. The one in the Torah's list of blemishes is dry both inside and outside. The one in the משנה is moist outside and inside. The Egyptian one is dry inside and moist outside, as it says: 'and it became a boil breaking out in blisters on man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the challenge by splitting גרב into three kinds. The 'moist' גרב in the דברים פסוק is the Egyptian kind, which is moist only on the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's blemish is dry inside and out, so it never heals. The משנה's kind is moist inside and out, so it heals and is not a blemish. The Egyptian kind looks moist outside but is dry inside, so it does not heal, and that is why the פסוק says it cannot be healed.

keyTerms.meaning: blisters, oozing bubbles (a sign of wetness)

steps.whatToRemember: Three kinds of גרב: Torah blemish = dry inside and out (no healing). משנה = moist inside and out (heals, not a blemish). Egypt = dry inside, moist outside (no healing). What matters for healing is the inside.

phrases.english: Rather, there are three kinds:

phrases.aramaic: דִּקְרָא — יָבֵשׁ בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: the one of the verse is dry both on the inside and on the outside;
the one of the Mishnah is moist on the outside and on the inside;
the one of Egypt is dry on the inside and moist on the outside,
as it is written: 'And it became a boil'
'breaking out in blisters on man.'
phrases.notes: The blisters ooze, which shows the Egyptian boil is moist on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into categories (three types instead of two)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There were only two kinds of גרב, moist and dry, so moist גרב from the פסוק must not heal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'moist' גרב of Egypt is moist only outside and dry inside, so it does not heal. The משנה's גרב is moist through and through, so it heals.

steps.title: Where do we learn the old, sick, and foul-smelling animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'and the old one, the sick one, and the foul-smelling one.' Where do we learn these from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, about animals that are not true blemishes but still may not be brought as a קרבן. It asks for the source and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These conditions are not on the Torah's list of blemishes, yet the משנה disqualifies them. So the גמרא needs to find where the Torah excludes them.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these things learned?

phrases.english: 'And the old, and the sick, and the foul-smelling.'
From where are these things learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that disqualifies old, sick, and foul-smelling animals

steps.title: Three uses of 'from' exclude the three animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the three times the word 'מן' appears in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'From the flock, from the sheep, and from the goats.' This excludes the old, the sick, and the foul-smelling animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Each 'מן' in the פסוק teaches one exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מן' means 'some of,' not all of the flock. The פסוק says it three times, so it removes three kinds of animals: old, sick, and foul-smelling.

keyTerms.meaning: from, some of (a word that limits)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'From the flock, and from the sheep, and from the goats.'
This excludes the old, the sick, and the foul-smelling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three 'מן' in ויקרא א:י exclude the old, sick, and foul-smelling animal.

steps.title: Why the Torah had to exclude both old and sick
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we cannot learn old from sick or sick from old. Each needs its own exclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah excluded only old, I would think that is because an old animal will never be healthy again, but a sick one can get better, so it would be allowed. If the Torah excluded only sick, I would think that is because being sick is not normal, but growing old is normal, so an old animal would be allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that each exclusion teaches something new. It explains why the Torah could not write just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old has a stronger reason to be excluded because it is permanent. Sick has a stronger reason because it is not natural. Each has a reason the other lacks, so neither can be learned from the other, and both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: they are needed (each teaches something new)

steps.whatToRemember: This is a צריכותא. Old is permanent, sick is unnatural. Each has its own reason, so the Torah had to write both.

phrases.english: And they are both needed,
for if the Torah had written only to exclude an old one,
which will not become healthy again,
but a sick one, which can become healthy again,
I would say it is not excluded.
And if it had written only to exclude a sick one,
because that is not its natural way,
but an old one, since that is its natural way,
I would say it is not excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the separate exclusions in Step 17 are each needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exclusions of old and sick are each needed, because each has a reason for disqualification that the other lacks (permanence or unnaturalness).

steps.title: Why all three exclusions are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. Two exclusions alone would cover only weak animals and miss the מזוהם. One exclusion alone would cover only the מזוהם and miss the weak animals. So all three are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only two exclusions, we would say they exclude these weak animals (old and sick). But a foul-smelling animal, which is not weak, we would say is not excluded. And if the תורה had written only one exclusion for the foul-smelling animal, because it is disgusting, we would say the old and sick animals, which are not disgusting, are not excluded. So all three are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes proving that all three exclusions are needed. Each one covers a different kind of flaw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old and sick animals share one problem: they are weak (כחוש). A מזוהם animal has a different problem: it is disgusting (מאוס), even though it is strong. Because the reasons are different, you cannot learn one from the other, so the תורה had to write all three.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a bad smell
They are needed (all of them are necessary)
I would have said no (it is not included)

steps.whatToRemember: Old and sick animals are excluded because they are weak. A מזוהם animal is excluded because it is disgusting. These are two different reasons, so each needs its own exclusion.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only two,
they would exclude these, which are weak (old and sick),
phrases.notes: Old and sick both mean a weak animal.

phrases.english: but a foul-smelling one, which is not weak —
I would say it is not excluded.
And also, if it only excluded the foul-smelling one
because it is disgusting,
but these (old and sick), which are not disgusting —
I would say they are not excluded.
So they are all needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא started in step 18, now bringing in the מזוהם case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three exclusions from 'מן' are needed, because weakness and disgustingness are different reasons for disqualifying an animal.

steps.title: Source for an animal used for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, an animal used for a sin, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And an animal with which a sin was done, etc.' What is the source for this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case in the משנה and asks where the rule comes from. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that an animal used for a sin cannot be brought as a קרבן. The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin was done with it (the animal was used for a sin)
From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: The Mishnah said: 'And one with which a sin was done, etc.'
From where do we know these things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה, the same way step 16 did.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוק for disqualifying an animal used for a sin.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads each 'מן' as an exclusion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the phrases in ויקרא 1:2 as exclusions: רובע and נרבע, נעבד, מוקצה, and נוגח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'From the animal' excludes an animal that lay with a person and an animal that a person lay with. 'From the cattle' excludes an animal worshipped as a god. 'From the flock' excludes an animal set aside for idol worship. 'And from the flock' excludes an animal that gored and killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Each phrase in the פסוק about bringing a קרבן excludes one more kind of animal tied to a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מן' ('from') means 'some, but not all,' so each time it appears it removes a group of animals. The extra 'ו' in 'ומן הצאן' adds one more exclusion, the animal that gored. Every animal on this list is linked to a serious sin.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that lay with a person
An animal that a person lay with
An animal worshipped as an idol
An animal set aside for idol worship
An animal that gored (and killed) a person

steps.confusionAlert: מוקצה here does NOT mean the שבת idea of things you may not move. Here it means an animal set aside for עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'From the animal' — to exclude one that lay with a person and one that a person lay with,
'From the cattle' — to exclude one that was worshipped,
'From the flock' — to exclude one set aside for idol worship,
'And from the flock' — to exclude one that gored.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 1:2: each 'מן' and the extra 'ו' exclude רובע, נרבע, נעבד, מוקצה, and נוגח from being brought as a קרבן.

steps.title: These animals are killed anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רובע, נרבע, and נוגח are put to death anyway, so why does the תורה need a פסוק to stop them from being brought as a קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But these animals are liable to be killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא. If these animals must be stoned anyway, it makes no sense to need a פסוק saying not to bring them as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal involved in רביעה or one that killed a person is sentenced to סקילה. An animal that must be killed could never be brought on the מזבח anyway, so the exclusion looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: But these are liable to be killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exclusions of רובע, נרבע, and נוגח in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These animals are stoned anyway, so a פסוק excluding them from being a קרבן seems pointless.

steps.title: Known through only one witness or the owner
steps.stepSummary: The case is where only one witness or the owner says what happened. That is not enough to kill the animal, but it is enough to disqualify it as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where it is known through one witness or through the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is speaking about a case with no two witnesses. So the animal is not killed, but it still cannot be brought as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To kill an animal, a בית דין needs two עדים. One witness, or the owner's own word, is not enough for סקילה. It is still enough to disqualify the animal from the מזבח, which is exactly what the משנה says.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the phrase 'על פי עד אחד או על פי הבעלים' in the משנה. Being too weak to kill the animal is still strong enough to disqualify it as a קרבן.
steps.whatToRemember: The animal is not killed, because there are not two witnesses. But it is still פסול for the מזבח, based on one witness or the owner.

phrases.english: It is based on one witness
or based on the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These animals are always killed, so the exclusion is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: With only one witness or the owner, the animal is not killed, but it is still disqualified as a קרבן.

steps.title: Why the rule makes sense for a טומטום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a טומטום can never be slaughtered. In the מקדש it might be female. Outside it might be a male with no מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a טומטום. It cannot be slaughtered in the מקדש, because maybe it is female. It cannot be slaughtered in the country, because maybe it is male and has no blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה and first explains the easy case, the טומטום. This is a setup line: it prepares a question about the אנדרוגינוס in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female is not a בכור, so it cannot be offered in the מקדש. A male בכור with no מום is holy, so it cannot be slaughtered outside. Since a טומטום might be either one, it is stuck both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (sets up a contrast)
An animal whose gender cannot be seen because the organs are covered
The country, meaning outside the מקדש
A blemish that disqualifies an animal from the מזבח

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding a tumtum:
not in the Temple,
since perhaps it is a female;
not in the country,

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא זָכָר הוּא וְלֵית בֵּהּ מוּמָא.
phrases.english: since perhaps it is a male and it has no blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה (טומטום and אנדרוגינוס)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום is doubtful both ways, so it can be slaughtered neither in the מקדש nor outside.

steps.title: Shouldn't the אנדרוגינוס count as blemished?
steps.stepSummary: An אנדרוגינוס cannot go in the מקדש because it might be female. But outside, even if it is male, its female organ should count as a 'crack' (חריץ). That is a מום, so it should be allowed to be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an אנדרוגינוס? Granted it cannot be slaughtered in the מקדש, because maybe it is female. But in the country too? Say it is male. Its female organ should count as a crack, and one should slaughter it because of that blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that an אנדרוגינוס cannot be slaughtered even outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists חרוץ (cracked) as a מום. The female organ looks like a crack in the body. If it counts, then every male אנדרוגינוס is a בעל מום and may be slaughtered outside, which goes against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with both male and female organs

phrases.english: But a hermaphrodite?
Granted, not in the Temple,
since perhaps it is a female.
But in the country also?
Granted that it is a male,
let the female organ be considered a crack,
and let one slaughter it on account of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the טומטום reasoning as a contrast to question the אנדרוגינוס
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an אנדרוגינוס may not be slaughtered outside the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is male, its female organ should be a חרוץ-type מום, which would permit slaughter outside.

steps.title: אביי: a crack must be on a bone
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the פסוק puts חרוץ next to שבור. Just as a break happens only on a bone, a crack counts as a מום only on a bone. A slit in soft flesh does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says 'or cracked or broken.' Cracked is like broken. Just as broken is on a bone, so cracked is on a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by narrowing what the תורה means by חרוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two words appear together, אביי learns one from the other. A bone can break but flesh cannot. So חרוץ also means a crack in bone. The female organ is in flesh, so it is not a מום.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The verse says: 'Or cracked or broken,'
cracked is similar to broken:
just as broken is in the place of a bone,
so too cracked is in the place of a bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא on the אנדרוגינוס
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the definition of a term through a nearby word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any crack, even in flesh, counts as חרוץ
steps.terutzMaskana: חרוץ is only a crack in bone, so the female organ is not a מום

steps.title: רבא: a crack in flesh is not a blemish anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even without the comparison to שבור, a crack in flesh cannot be a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without 'broken,' you cannot say that a crack in the place of flesh is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same question. He does not need אביי's word comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reaches the same result as אביי: a crack in flesh is not a מום. His source is different, and he proves it in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even without 'broken,'
you cannot say
that a crack in the place of flesh is a blemish,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא, without relying on אביי's source
steps.terutzMaskana: A crack in flesh is never a מום

steps.title: רבא's proof begins: גרב is already a crack in skin
steps.stepSummary: If a crack in flesh were a מום, then גרב would already be included in חרוץ. The ברייתא explained גרב as חרס, hard boils, and that is a crack in the skin. The פסוק about skin looking 'deeper than the skin' shows that such a condition looks like a crack. Step 29 finishes the argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought it is a blemish: the ברייתא said that 'גרב' is חרס, and that is a crack. As it is written, 'and its appearance is deeper than the skin,' like the look of sunlight, which seems deeper than the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts proving his claim. He shows that גרב is basically a crack in the skin. The step ends before the punchline, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point being built: if any crack in flesh counted as חרוץ, the תורה would not need to list גרב as its own separate מום. To show that חרס/גרב is a 'crack,' רבא borrows how חז״ל read the נגעים פסוק. A spot can look sunken, the way a sunlit area looks deeper than a shaded one.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you thought)
A skin condition listed as a מום

steps.confusionAlert: This step ends in the middle of רבא's argument. The 'so what' is that גרב would be extra if a flesh-crack were already a מום. Step 29 spells this out.

phrases.english: for if it would enter your mind that it is a blemish,
since he said 'garav' is ḥeres (hard boils),
it is indeed a crack,
as it is written: 'And its appearance is deeper than the skin,'
like the appearance of sunlight, which looks deeper than the shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רבא's claim
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a crack in flesh is not a מום
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא defining גרב as חרס, plus ויקרא 13:30 showing that such skin looks sunken or cracked

steps.title: Why the Torah needed to write 'גרב' separately
steps.stepSummary: רבא completes his proof. If a crack in flesh were a מום, the Torah would not need to write גרב, because a קל וחומר from חרוץ would teach it. Writing גרב shows that a crack in flesh is not a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a crack in flesh were a blemish, the Torah could have written only 'crack' and skipped 'גרב.' I would reason: if a crack, which is not disgusting, is a blemish, then גרב, which is disgusting, is surely a blemish. The Torah wrote 'גרב' anyway. This teaches that a crack in a place of flesh is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's proof from Step 28. The extra word גרב in the פסוק shows that a crack in soft flesh is not a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גרב (hard boils) is really a kind of crack in the skin, and it is also repulsive. If cracks in flesh already counted under חרוץ, a קל וחומר would cover גרב, and the Torah would not need to write it. Since the Torah did write it, cracks in flesh must not count as a מום on their own. That is why the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס does not count as a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳ who wrote it
'All the more so', a קל וחומר argument
In a place of soft flesh, where there is no bone

steps.whatToRemember: רבא proves from the extra word גרב that a crack in soft flesh is not a מום. This holds even without אביי's comparison to שבור.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the Torah wrote גרב only to teach about boils. רבא's point is that the Torah would not need to write גרב at all if cracks in flesh were already a מום. The extra word is what teaches the rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why an אנדרוגינוס בכור cannot be slaughtered outside the מקדש because of its female organ, according to the view the גמרא is defending.

phrases.english: Then let the Merciful One write 'crack'
and it would not need to write 'garav'
and I would say:
If 'crack', which is not repulsive, is a blemish,
phrases.notes: First half of the קל וחומר

phrases.english: then 'garav', which is repulsive, is it not all the more so?
The Merciful One wrote 'garav'
to say that a crack in a place of flesh
is not a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיכְתֹּב רַחֲמָנָא חָרוּץ וְלָא בָּעֵי גָּרָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 28
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a crack in soft flesh is not a מום
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word גרב in the פסוק of blemishes, which a קל וחומר would otherwise make unnecessary

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל calls it the greatest blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי ישמעאל's words from the משנה. He says an אנדרוגינוס has the greatest מום of all, which seems to go against both אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: There is no blemish greater than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי ישמעאל from the משנה, who treats the אנדרוגינוס's female organ as a big מום. This sets up the next two steps, which explain how he can say this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא both just argued that a crack in flesh is not a מום. רבי ישמעאל says the opposite: it is the greatest מום, so the animal may be slaughtered. The גמרא now has to explain his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא in the משנה who disagrees about the אנדרוגינוס
'You have no blemish greater than this'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
You have no blemish greater than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: אֵין לְךָ מוּם גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a תנא whose ruling seems to contradict the conclusion of Steps 26-29
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of אביי and רבא that a crack in flesh is not a מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל treats the female organ, a crack in flesh, as the greatest מום, so he clearly does not hold like them.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה in step 8 attributes this line to רבי שמעון, while the גמרא here quotes it as רבי ישמעאל (versions of the text differ). It is the same statement about the אנדרוגינוס, so do not look for a new opinion.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל does not hold like אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי ישמעאל rejects אביי's comparison of חרוץ to שבור. For him, a crack does not need to be on a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not hold like אביי. We do not say that 'crack' is similar to 'broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל is not bothered by אביי's argument. He simply does not accept the comparison between חרוץ and שבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole point depended on reading חרוץ next to שבור, so that a crack must be on bone just like a break. רבי ישמעאל does not learn the two words from each other. So for him, a crack in soft flesh can still be a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Broken, a blemish that happens only on a bone
We do not say, we do not accept this reasoning

phrases.english: He does not hold like Abaye;
that 'crack' is similar to 'broken'
we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first part of the problem raised in Step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement with the derivation: רבי ישמעאל rejects אביי's reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone must accept that חרוץ is compared to שבור.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל does not compare them, so a crack in flesh can be a מום.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל does not hold like רבא either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי ישמעאל can limit רבא's rule. A crack in flesh that cannot be seen is not a מום, but a clearly visible one, like the female organ, is a 'מום רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also does not hold like רבא. Perhaps רבא's rule applies only where the crack is not noticeable. But where it is noticeable, we call it 'an ill blemish.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי ישמעאל avoids רבא's proof from גרב. He narrows it to cracks that are not visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא proved from גרב that a crack in flesh is not a מום. רבי ישמעאל can say that this proof only covers cracks that are not conspicuous. A visible crack, like the female organ of an אנדרוגינוס, falls under the general words 'מום רע', so it is a real מום and the בכור may be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'An ill blemish', a general phrase in the פסוק (דברים טו:כא)
'I read it as', I apply this פסוק to it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל disagrees with both explanations. Against אביי, he does not compare חרוץ to שבור. Against רבא, he limits the גרב proof to cracks you cannot see. A visible crack in flesh, like the female organ, is a 'מום רע'.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל does not say every crack in flesh is a מום. He only says a visible one is. The hidden kind can still fit רבא's proof.

phrases.english: He also does not hold like Rava;
perhaps that applies where it is not noticeable,
but where it is noticeable,
I apply to it the words 'an ill blemish.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second part of the problem raised in Step 30, following Step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבא's proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's proof from גרב rules out every crack in flesh as a מום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof covers only cracks that are not visible. A visible crack is a 'מום רע'.
